decisions.statement: A warrant is handed one path and answers with the readings that path owes.
A warrant states its reach on read.
A warrant states its reach on write.
A warrant states whether the warrant is transitive.
A warrant running on neither read nor write has landed and has nobody.
Landing with neither reach on is how a warrant states its rule before that warrant binds anyone.
A warrant is not transitive unless the warrant says so.
A warrant takes and gives paths under the root the warrant was given.
Every warrant that runs is a page here.
No file names a warrant by hand.

definition: a module naming what a change to a file requires its writer to have read

directives.name: Alan Approves Warrants
directives.act: Add a warrant to akasha only where Alan has approved that warrant.
directives.warrant: A warrant binds every writer on every change, and a wrong one stops work it should not.
aids: Approving the initiative is not approving a warrant.
A warrant replacing an old one still needs approval.
Widening what an approved warrant reaches needs none.
How an approved warrant reads needs none.
